conventions.convention: The ambient manifold is smooth, time-oriented, four-dimensional and Lorentzian with signature (-,+,+,+). Future causal vectors pair negatively with the supplied timelike field N. The connection is torsion-free and metric-compatible.
The generator k is smooth, nowhere zero, future-directed, spans the radical of the induced hypersurface metric, and satisfies ∇k k=0. The screen is k⊥/Rk; B([X],[Y])=g(∇X k,Y), θ=tr B, and σ=B−θḡ/2.
Curvature is R(X,Y)Z=∇X∇Y Z−∇Y∇X Z−∇[X,Y] Z, with R(∂c,∂d)∂b=Rᵃ_bcd∂a and Ric_bd=Rᵃ_bad.

The area theorem assumes Countable Choice, a compact spacelike initial cut, and a smooth affine flow for every λ≥λ₀ whose cuts remain embedded and spacelike. Null convergence holds throughout this full future flow. Area uses intrinsic densities without an orientation.

The parameter domain is P={(m,a,q):m>0, m²>a²+q²}. The square root s is positive, r₊=m+s, D=r₊²+a², j=ma, κ=s/D, Ω=a/D and Φ=qr₊/D. These mathematical functions receive no physical units or thermodynamic identification here.
Signed surface gravity uses the ambient-covector equation d(g(χ,χ))=−2κχ♭ for the specified Killing generator; rescaling that generator changes its normalization.

Fixed (a,q) means dj=a dm and retains the angular work term. The work-free restriction fixes (j,q), parametrized by a=j₀/m on the stated nonempty interval m>m₀. Extremal values are boundary data, not open-family differential identities.
The cone starts at r₀>0 with λ₀=−r₀, uses λ=t, and has cuts only for λ₀≤λ<0; thus every cut satisfies t+r=0 and the finite future vertex is excluded.

load_bearing.statement: Defines a smooth embedded null hypersurface, a smooth future affine null generator, the quotient screen k⊥/Rk, its candidate metric and deformation form, expansion and shear; independently defines the smooth Kerr–Newman parameter functions on P={(m,a,q):m>0, m²>a²+q²}.

For a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, a smooth null hypersurface and its smooth affine null generator, the screen spaces form a smooth rank-two real vector bundle; the induced screen metric is representative-independent and positive definite, and B is a representative-independent smooth bilinear form.

Assuming Countable Choice, the stated smooth future affine null flow from a compact spacelike transverse cut, persistent embedded spacelike cuts for all λ≥λ₀, and Ric(k,k)≥0 throughout that flow, θ≥0 on every cut, A′(λ)=∫Sλ θ dA≥0 for λ>λ₀, and A(λ₂)≥A(λ₁) whenever λ₂≥λ₁≥λ₀.

On the strict family P, dm=κ dA/(8π)+Ω dj+Φ dq and m=κA/(4π)+2Ωj+Φq. At fixed (a,q), κ dA/(8π)=(r₊²/D)dm; at fixed (j,q), dm=κ dA/(8π)=T_b dS_b,s*, with T_b=bκ and S_b,s*=A/(8πb)+s*. The geometric product determines neither the scale b>0 nor the additive offset.

For the selected ingoing KN model with a=q=0 and m=M>0, r=2m is a null Killing horizon for the future generator ∂v, with signed surface gravity 1/(4m), round-section area 16πm², and zero angular-velocity, potential and angular-momentum parameter functions.

concerns.concern: Proof step 3.2 passes from the intrinsic density integral to the parameter-integral supplier without stating the integration bridge. The density definition uses Riemann integrals of zero-extended chart coefficients, whereas lem-em-parameter-integrals explicitly uses Lebesgue integrals. Here the bridge is immediate: each zero extension is smooth with compact support, so its Riemann and Lebesgue integrals agree, and it vanishes outside K_i; the same applies to its parameter derivative. State or cite this identification to make the supplier application explicit.
